question:
Consider the following about India’s Ramsar Sites:

1. India has the largest number of Ramsar sites in South Asia.

2. Keibul Lamjao, the world’s only floating national park, is also designated as a Ramsar site.

3. Every Ramsar site in India is located along the coastline.

Which of the statements above are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 2 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **India has the largest number of Ramsar sites in South Asia**, with over 98 wetlands designated under the Ramsar Convention as of 2026.
 
• The Ramsar Convention, signed in 1971 in Ramsar, Iran, is an international treaty for the conservation and wise use of wetlands.
 
• **Keibul Lamjao National Park in Manipur**, which is the world’s only floating national park, is also designated as a Ramsar site. It is located on Loktak Lake, which is a Ramsar site due to its ecological importance.
 
• Ramsar sites are recognized for their ecological significance and are protected under the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017, in India.
 
• Not all Ramsar sites in India are located along the coastline; many are inland wetlands, such as Chilika Lake in Odisha and Sambhar Lake in Rajasthan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Statement 3: Every Ramsar site in India is located along the coastline** - This statement is incorrect. India’s Ramsar sites include both coastal and inland wetlands. Examples of inland Ramsar sites are Wular Lake in Jammu & Kashmir, Bhoj Wetland in Madhya Pradesh, and Nalsarovar Bird Sanctuary in Gujarat.
 
• **Importance of Ramsar Sites:**
 
 
• Ramsar sites are wetlands of international importance designated under the Ramsar Convention.
 
• They play a critical role in biodiversity conservation, groundwater recharge, and providing livelihoods to millions of people.
 
 
 
• **About Keibul Lamjao National Park:**
 
 
• Keibul Lamjao is located in Manipur, within Loktak Lake, which is a Ramsar site.
 
• The park is famous for its floating biomass called “phumdi” and is the last natural habitat of the endangered Sangai deer (Rucervus eldii eldii).
 
 
 
• **India’s Ramsar Initiative:**
 
 
• India actively participates in the Ramsar Convention and has implemented several wetland conservation programs to protect these sites.
 
• The number of Ramsar sites in India has steadily increased over the years, demonstrating commitment to wetland conservation.
